topic: ハナおばあちゃん's legend of New Year's Eve soba
title_jp: {隼人|はやと}さまと{年越し|としこし}そば
context: Thursday 31 December, New Year's Eve: while ハナおばあちゃん teaches アルちゃん and {颯太|そうた} to make soba, アルちゃん reads her column in the New Year issue of the town newsletter: the legend of how {黒鉄隼人|くろがねはやと} started {鷹ノ原|たかのはら}'s New Year's Eve soba.
scene: New Year's Eve. While the soba dough rests, you read ハナおばあちゃん's column in the town newsletter: why {鷹ノ原|たかのはら} eats soba tonight.
text_title: {町報|ちょうほう|town newsletter|2}たかのはら{新年号|しんねんごう|New Year issue|2}：ハナさんのむかし{話|ばなし}

phrases.jp: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると、{今夜|こんや}は{雪|ゆき}が{降る|ふる}そうです。
phrases.en: According to the forecast, it's going to snow tonight.
phrases.note: 〜によると + 〜そうです: the classic pair for passing on what you heard.

phrases.jp: {昔|むかし}はお{米|こめ}がほとんど{取れなかった|とれなかった|to be harvested|3}そうだよ。
phrases.en: Apparently they could hardly grow any rice in the old days.

phrases.jp: そばは{細く|ほそく|thin|4}{長く|ながく}、{長生き|ながいき}できるようにって{意味|いみ}なんだって。
phrases.en: Apparently soba means 'thin and long': so you'll live a long life.
phrases.note: 〜んだって = casual 'I heard'. Very common in speech.
Only before New Year. From 1 January it's あけましておめでとう.

phrases.jp: {除夜の鐘|じょやのかね|New Year's Eve temple bells|3}、{聞き|きき}に{行こう|いこう}か。
phrases.en: Shall we go and hear the New Year's Eve bells?

dialogue_setting: The 田中 kitchen, the afternoon of 31 December. Flour everywhere, and the town newsletter open on the table.

dialogue.speaker: Title
dialogue.jp: {黒鉄隼人|くろがねはやと}と{年越し|としこし|seeing the old year out|3}そば
dialogue.en: {黒鉄隼人|くろがねはやと} and the New Year's Eve soba

dialogue.speaker: Story 1
dialogue.jp: {天明|てんめい}の{飢饉|ききん|famine|2}のあと、{鷹ノ原|たかのはら}の{村|むら}は{貧しく|まずしく|poor|3}、お{米|こめ}がほとんど{取れなかった|とれなかった|to be harvested|3}そうだ。
dialogue.en: After the Tenmei famine, {鷹ノ原|たかのはら} village was poor, and they say it could hardly grow any rice.

dialogue.speaker: Story 2
dialogue.jp: でも{寒い|さむい}{山|やま}の{畑|はたけ|field|3}でも{育つ|そだつ}そばが、{人々|ひとびと}の{命|いのち|life|3}を{救った|すくった|to save, rescue|3}という。
dialogue.en: But buckwheat, which grows even in cold mountain fields, is said to have saved people's lives.

dialogue.speaker: Story 3
dialogue.jp: {大晦日|おおみそか|New Year's Eve|3}の{夜|よる}、{隼人|はやと}さまは{峠|とうげ|mountain pass|2}の{小屋|こや|hut, cabin|3}でそばを{打ち|うち|to make (noodles) by hand|3}、{村|むら}の{子|こ}どもたちに{配った|くばった}そうだ。
dialogue.en: On New Year's Eve, they say, {隼人|はやと}さま made soba in his hut on the pass and shared it with the village children.

dialogue.speaker: 隼人
dialogue.jp: 「{細く|ほそく|thin|4}{長く|ながく}{生きる|いきる|to live|4}のじゃ。{来年|らいねん}も{皆|みな}で{食べよう|たべよう}ぞ」
dialogue.en: 'Live thin and long. Next year too, we shall all eat together!'
dialogue.note: Drama samurai speech. Modern: {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く{生|い}きるんだ。{来年|らいねん}もみんなで{食|た}べよう.

dialogue.speaker: Story 4
dialogue.jp: それから{村|むら}では、{大晦日|おおみそか}にそばを{食べる|たべる}ようになったそうだ。{本当|ほんとう}かどうかは、{知らん|しらん}けどね。
dialogue.en: From then on, they say, the village began eating soba on New Year's Eve. Whether it's true, I couldn't tell you.
dialogue.note: {知|し}らん = {知|し}らない (casual, older speech).

dialogue.speaker: Sign-off
dialogue.jp: {皆|みな}さんも{細く|ほそく}{長く|ながく}、よいお{年|とし}を。（{山本|やまもと}ハナ）
dialogue.en: Everyone, live thin and long, and have a good New Year. ({山本|やまもと} ハナ)

listening.intro: That evening, a voice message from レン.

lines.jp: レンです。{今|いま}、{実家|じっか}で{葵|あおい}と{紅白|こうはく|NHK's New Year's Eve song show|3}{見てる|みてる}よ。
lines.en: It's レン. I'm at my parents' place watching Kōhaku with {葵|あおい}.

lines.jp: 3{日|か}、{楽しみ|たのしみ}にしてるね。よいお{年|とし}を。
lines.en: Looking forward to the 3rd. Have a good New Year.

listening.question: レンは{今|いま}、どこにいますか。
listening.explain: {実家|じっか}で = at his parents' home, watching {紅白|こうはく} with his sister.

grammar.form: verb: plain form + そうだ ({取|と}れなかったそうだ, {配|くば}ったそうだ, {降|ふ}るそうだ) · い-adj: + そうだ ({寒|さむ}いそうだ) · な-adj / noun: + だそうだ ({有名|ゆうめい}だそうだ, {雪|ゆき}だそうだ)
grammar.explanation: Passes on something you heard or read: 'apparently, they say'. Often with 〜によると for the source. Don't mix it up with stem + そう ('looks like'): {降|ふ}りそう = looks like snow, {降|ふ}るそうだ = I hear it'll snow. It never goes past: not そうだった.

examples.jp: {健太|けんた}の{彼女|かのじょ}は、{看護師|かんごし}だそうです。
examples.en: Apparently {健太|けんた}'s girlfriend is a nurse.

examples.jp: {隼人|はやと}は、{和歌|わか|classical poem|2}が{下手|へた}だったそうだ。
examples.en: They say {隼人|はやと} was bad at poetry.

quiz.question: ニュースによると、{明日|あした}は{大雪|おおゆき}＿＿。
quiz.en: According to the news, there'll be heavy snow tomorrow.
quiz.explain: A noun needs だ before hearsay そうだ: {大雪|おおゆき}だそうだ.

quiz_more.question: {天気予報|てんきよほう}で{聞いた|きいた}。{午後|ごご}から{雪|ゆき}が＿＿。
quiz_more.en: I heard it on the forecast: it'll snow from the afternoon.
quiz_more.explain: You heard it, so plain form + そうだ. {降|ふ}りそう is what you guess from the sky.

quiz_more.question: {隼人|はやと}は、そばが{大好き|だいすき}＿＿。
quiz_more.en: They say {隼人|はやと} loved soba.
quiz_more.explain: Put the past in front: {大好|だいす}きだった + そうだ. そうだ itself stays present.

kanji.where: Written on ハナおばあちゃん's bag of buckwheat flour: 「十割そば用」.
kanji.breakdown: {十割|じゅうわり}: 十 ten + 割 one tenth → 'ten tenths', all of it: soba with no wheat flour.
kanji.related: {二八|にはち}そば = 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat; {割引|わりびき} = discount.

tip.title: The last night of the year
tip.body: Eat {年越し|としこし}そば before midnight: leaving some for next year is thought unlucky. Temples ring the {除夜の鐘|じょやのかね} 108 times, once for each worldly desire, while many families watch NHK's {紅白歌合戦|こうはくうたがっせん}. Say よいお{年|とし}を until the 31st, then あけましておめでとう.

challenge.prompt: {由紀|ゆき}, at her parents' house, on LINE: 「{年越し|としこし}そばって、なんで{食べる|たべる}か{知ってる|しってる}？」 Pass on what you read: apparently it's so you live a long life.

options.jp: {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く{生|い}きられるように、{食|た}べるそうだよ。
options.why: Plain form {食|た}べる + そうだ passes on what you read; casual よ for a friend.

options.jp: {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く{生|い}きられるように、{食|た}べそうだよ。
options.why: Stem + そう means 'looks like it'll eat', not 'I heard'.

options.jp: {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く{生|い}きられるように、{食|た}べるそうだったよ。
options.why: Hearsay そうだ has no past form.

options.jp: {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く{生|い}きられるように、{食|た}べるそうでございます。
options.why: Hotel-level keigo: very odd with a friend on LINE.

challenge.hint: You read it: plain form + そうだ
challenge.model_answer: {細く|ほそく|thin|4}{長く|ながく}{生きられる|いきられる|to be able to live|4}ように、{食べる|たべる}そうだよ。
challenge.explanation: 〜ように = 'so that': so you can live thin and long. {食|た}べるそうだ is hearsay: you're passing on what ハナおばあちゃん wrote, not your own idea. Plain だよ keeps it casual for {由紀|ゆき}.

vocab.note: Written, a bit serious. In speech: お{金|かね}がない.

vocab.en: to be harvested; to come off
vocab.note: お{米|こめ}が{取|と}れる = rice can be grown. Also ボタンが{取|と}れた = a button came off.
Life itself. {命|いのち}の{恩人|おんじん} = someone who saved your life.
Big rescues and lives. Everyday 'help' is {助|たす}ける.
Every 31 December. みそか = last day of a month.
{山小屋|やまごや} = mountain hut for hikers.

vocab.en: to make (noodles) by hand; to hit
vocab.note: そばを{打|う}つ, うどんを{打|う}つ. Also: {打|う}つ = type, hit.
Opposite: {太|ふと}い. {細|ほそ}く{長|なが}く = modestly but for a long time.
Being alive. Living somewhere is {住|す}む.

kanji_study.parts: 求 to seek, ask for + 攵 act, strike → taking action for someone who is asking for help: rescue.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 球 (ball): 球 has 王 jewel on the left; 救 has 攵 on the right.

kanji_study.parts: 矛 a halberd + 攵 strike, act + 力 strength → putting all your strength into the task you're given: duty.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 努 (effort): 努 has 奴 on top of 力; 務 has 矛 and 攵.
